title: Add streaming HTML insertion methods
body: Introduce safe and unsafe streaming HTML parsing and insertion methods returning a `WritableStream`: * `Element` & `ShadowRoot`: `streamHTML()`, `streamHTMLUnsafe()`, `streamAppendHTML()`, `streamAppendHTMLUnsafe()`, `streamPrependHTML()`, and `streamPrependHTMLUnsafe()` * `NonDocumentTypeChildNode`: `streamBeforeHTML()`, `streamBeforeHTMLUnsafe()`, `streamAfterHTML()`, `streamAfterHTMLUnsafe()`, `streamReplaceWithHTML()`, and `streamReplaceWithHTMLUnsafe()` Key behaviors and parser updates: * **Stream operations**: `writeAlgorithm` and `closeAlgorithm` convert chunks to `DOMString`, append chunks (or an explicit `"EOF"` character on close) to the parser's input stream, and run the fragment parser. `closeAlgorithm` waits for any pending parser-blocking scripts via `fragment parser close promise`. `abortAlgorithm` aborts the fragment parser (deferring via `fragment parser abort requested` if currently running), marks open `script` elements on the stack as already started, and unblocks rendering on pending scripts. * **Displaced reference child**: If `referenceChild` is no longer a child of `target` when a node would be inserted before it or when another chunk is written, `invalid reference child steps` error the stream (and reject `fragment parser close promise` if closing) with a `"HierarchyRequestError"` `DOMException` and abort the fragment parser. Elements that would be inserted before a displaced `referenceChild` are created in the `appropriate template contents owner document` with a null custom element registry and dropped, and the adoption agency algorithm skips removing `lastNode`. * **Validation, Trusted Types & DOM mutations**: Target validation (throwing `"NotSupportedError"` for HTML/SVG `script` context elements, or `"HierarchyRequestError"` for `html` targets or invalid `parent for HTML streaming`), `HTMLTemplateElement` redirection to `template contents`, and Trusted Types / `SanitizerConfig` validation occur synchronously before returning the stream or mutating the DOM. * **Scripts, custom elements & fragment parsing**: - Extracts `initialize an HTML fragment parser`. When `runScripts` is true, `script target document` is `context`'s node document; otherwise it is the temporary inert document. - Parser-blocking, `defer`, `async`, and module scripts follow normal HTML parser pausing and execution order. - Custom element upgrades/callbacks when inserting into a connected target run before any subsequent `script` via a dedicated element queue; other reactions when streaming HTML use the backup element queue. - The speculative HTML parser is not started in the fragment case. Speculative fetches from the fragment parser are still allowed, except when sanitizing or for elements that will be dropped. *The end* (`stops parsing`) returns early for fragment parsers. - Elements whose intended parent is the fragment root `html` element are created directly in the target's (or fragment's) node document. - SVG `script` elements are only processed when the parser's `script target document` is not the parser's `Document` and the `script` element is connected (which also applies to document parsing when an ancestor of an SVG `script` was disconnected before ``). - Elements removed or replaced with their children by the sanitizer are created in the `appropriate template contents owner document` with a null custom element registry and not inserted into the DOM. Their descendants look up a null registry from them too. This also applies to the non-streaming methods that use the HTML fragment parsing algorithm with a sanitizer (`setHTML()`, `setHTMLUnsafe()`, etc.), where previously the whole fragment was parsed (and custom elements upgraded) before sanitization. Note: Pre-existing adoption agency algorithm edge cases (#13093) are out of scope for this PR. Closes #2142 - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Chrome * Gecko (https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1370) - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/61748 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/581018331 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=315741 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2043150 - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [ ] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: Will be done as part of Blink shipping - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
